pages.title: Dataset v2 (3000 zoomed 640x640 images): every sampled parameter
pages.intro: DATASET NOT YET GENERATED. Plan confirmed with the zoomed 640x640 revision (ADR 0016: native 640x640 crop, mine scale 0.25-0.40 in 4 linear bins, scene zoom coupling, 0-4 mines). Every graph on this page is the planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (scripts/generate_dataset.py --plan-only). Stratified factors are evenly sampled: equal-count buckets per image, value uniform inside the bucket, buckets crossed with each other by a balanced design. Everything else is randomized with the generator's tuned distributions. Before / after pairs use the same seed and change only the named parameter.

glossary.stratified: Evenly sampled: the range is cut into buckets and every bucket gets exactly the same number of images (or a fixed quota); the value is random inside it.
glossary.randomized: Each image / mine draws the value independently (i.i.d.) from the configured distribution.
glossary.balanced design: Bucket columns are shuffled, then rows are swapped inside a column to make every pair of factors as evenly crossed as possible (pairwise chi-square minimised); marginal counts never change.
glossary.chi-square: Sum over table cells of (count - expected)^2 / expected; 0 = perfectly even crossing.
glossary.PSF: Point-spread function: how the lens smears a point (here a Gaussian blur).
glossary.YOLO label: One line per box: class x_centre y_centre width height, normalised to 0-1.
glossary.native crop: Cutting a window out of the rendered image pixel for pixel (no resize or interpolation), so nothing gets blurred or stretched.
glossary.zoom coupling: Scaling everything physical (rocks, debris, ground texture, soil details) with the mine size, as if the camera moved closer.

tables.title: Decisions
rows: 640x640 JPEG as a NATIVE crop of the 1920x1080 render (no resize, no resampling); the window position is uniform and every mine is placed fully inside it (8 px margin); labels normalised to the crop
4 LINEAR bins over 0.25-0.40 (750 images each, uniform inside the bucket), mine length ~107-171 px; was 5 log bins over 0.10-0.40

rocks, grass clippings, leaf clumps, dirt and the mine's pixel-sized soil / contact details x z = scale / 0.2, debris counts x z^-2, background magnified by z (capped at 1.5 px per source px); blades follow px/mm; sensor effects stay in pixels (SCENE_ZOOM_COUPLING, default off in the generator)
3000 images (2700 train / 300 val), 6000 planned mines (2059 buried), 600 empty
mines per image (5), mine scale (4 linear bins), burial fraction (4), sun elevation (6), light: overcast + 4 shadow bins (5), background family (2, + per-file quotas), lens blur (3)
sun azimuth, all per-mine pose / face-down / colour / burial yes-no / dust / soft grains / position, camera jitter, debris counts, crop position
35 % of mines buried (random), target fraction in 4 equal-count buckets [0.05, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5], cap 0.5
generator-sampled 70-95 per image (an augmentation), saved at 640x640
output_dataset/v2_3000 (gitignored): images/{train,val}, labels/{train,val}, meta/, manifest.csv, data.yaml, plan/, README.md; the earlier 1920x1080 render was deleted
~0.7-2 s per image single-process (the full scene is still rendered at 1920x1080, fewer debris objects) -> roughly 15-25 min with 4 low-priority workers
the lead starts the render after the review of docs/zoomed_look.png

features.title: Mines per image
features.summary: How many PFM-1 mines are placed in the 640x640 crop (rejection sampling inside the crop, 50 attempts).
facts: Exact quota: 600 images (20 %) with 0 mines and 600 with each of 1..4 (user decision for the zoomed 640x640 dataset; was 0-8 with 600 / 300 x 8).

figure.label: Mines per image
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated).

features.notes: Planned mines in total: 6000. 4 mines of up to 171 px fit easily in the 624x624 placement area; the rendered manifest will record placed vs planned.

features.title: Mine scale (altitude)
features.summary: Mine size in the frame (proxy for flight altitude). The ground blade scale (px per mm) and the zoom coupling factor (scale / 0.2) come from the same bucket, so grass, rocks, debris and mines agree in scale.
facts: Each image gets one of 4 equal-width buckets (750 images per bucket); every mine in it draws its scale uniformly inside that bucket, i.e. uniform 0.25-0.40 overall (user decision: was 5 log bins over 0.1-0.4, where mines were often barely visible).

figure.label: Mine scale (altitude)
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated). Dotted lines: bucket edges; dashed orange: equal-count target.

before_after.label: Scale 0.25 vs 0.40
before_after.caption: Smallest vs largest end of the range, both zoom-coupled. native-resolution 640x640 px crop around the mine.

features.notes: Per-image buckets mean all mines in one image share a scale range (like one flight altitude). Mine counts per bucket are exact because the n_mines x scale table is balanced.

features.title: Burial fraction (target)
features.summary: How much of a buried mine is hidden under soil (3D clip by a tilted ground plane + wavy soil line, berm, clods).
facts: Each image gets one of 4 fraction buckets (750 images each); every mine is buried with the tuned probability 0.35 (random) and, if buried, draws its target fraction inside the image's bucket. Hard cap BURIAL_MAX_FRACTION 0.5 (render retries if the cap is exceeded).

figure.label: Burial fraction (target)
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated). Dotted lines: bucket edges; dashed orange: equal-count target.

before_after.label: Not buried vs 45% buried
before_after.caption: Same mine, fraction 0.45 (top bucket). native-resolution 640x640 px crop around the mine.

before_after.label: 15% vs 45% buried
before_after.caption: Lowest vs highest bucket. native-resolution 640x640 px crop around the mine.

features.notes: Buckets are [0.05, 0.2), [0.2, 0.3), [0.3, 0.4), [0.4, 0.5]: the first is wider, so the lightest burials get slightly less density per 0.01 than in the old uniform 0.05-0.5. The achieved hidden fraction is measured after rendering (it differs a little from the target). Images per bucket are exact (750); buried MINES per bucket vary a little (graph) because burial yes / no stays random per mine.

features.title: Background zoom
features.summary: Zoom-crop into the ground photo on top of scale-to-cover (texture scale).
facts: BG_ZOOM 1.0-2.0, then x mine scale / 0.2, capped at 1.5 output px per source px

Uniform BG_ZOOM per image, random offset; zoom coupling multiplies it by z (camera closer), but the magnification (output px per photo px) is capped at max(1.5, uncoupled value) so the texture does not get blurrier than the generator already allowed; upscaling uses bicubic interpolation.

features.title: Ground scale (px per mm)
features.summary: Size of grass blades / tufts / wisps (specified in mm) on screen.
facts: Drawn per image inside the image's mine-scale bucket (not separately planned).

figure.label: Ground scale (px per mm)
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated). Dotted lines: bucket edges; dashed orange: equal-count target.

features.notes: In the default generator this value is drawn independently of the mines' scale, so blades could be drawn at a different 'altitude' than the mines of the same image; the per-image scale bucket keeps the two within one bucket.

features.title: Scene zoom coupling (camera closer)
features.summary: Like moving the camera closer: rocks, grass clippings, leaf clumps, dirt snippets and specks are drawn z times larger and z^2 times rarer (same density per ground area); the mine's contact band, contact AO, berm lip, exposed-part AO, soil-grain size and soft-grain blur grow by z; the background texture is magnified by z (capped, see 'Background zoom'). Grass blades are sized in mm and already follow px/mm. Sensor effects (PSF, motion blur, noise, aberration shift, vignette, JPEG) stay in pixels.
facts: z = the image's mine scale / 0.2 (0.2 = the old plan's median scale), so it follows the scale bucket.

figure.label: Scene zoom coupling (camera closer)
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated). Dotted lines: bucket edges; dashed orange: equal-count target.

before_after.caption: Same mine size: without coupling rocks, clippings and the ground texture keep the old pixel size, so the mine looks out of scale. native-resolution 640x640 px crop around the mine.

features.notes: Default OFF in controlPanel (existing seeds and the earlier outputs are bit-identical with it off); the dataset driver turns it on. Debris count rounding and the crop window use new random streams R(11) / R(12) / R(13), so no existing stream changes.

features.title: Native 640x640 crop
features.summary: The saved image: a 640x640 window cut out of the 1920x1080 render without any resize or resampling. Labels are converted to the crop's normalised YOLO coordinates (a box crossing the edge would be clipped and kept only if visible pixels remain inside, the usual label policy; with the margin none do). The camera model (blur with a context pad, noise, colour, vignette) is applied to the crop as the camera's frame.
facts: Uniform window position per image (own stream R(11)), drawn before the mines; every mine is then placed fully inside the window (8 px margin).

figure.label: Native 640x640 crop
figure.caption: Planned distribution from the 3000-row sampling plan (dataset not yet generated).

before_after.after_label: saved 640x640 image (native pixels), red = YOLO boxes
before_after.caption: Plan row rendered with OUTPUT_CROP; the full frame on the left is the same scene re-rendered without the crop (mines pinned at the same positions).
